title: The tangent Proj of a geometric node is its quadratic normalization residue algebra
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, let $C$ be a scheme locally of finite type over $k$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], equidimensional of dimension one [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], and let $x\in C$ be a closed point. Suppose $\kappa=\kappa(x)$ is finite separable over $k$ [def-weil-residue-field, def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]. Assume $x$ is a geometric ordinary double point: for an algebraic closure $ ar k$ and a point $ ar x\in C_{ ar k}$ over $x$, the completed local ring is $ ar k[[u,v]]/(uv)$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure, def-pc-fibre-product, def-weil-pbc-adic-completion, def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Put $A=\mathcal O_{C,x}$, $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak m_x$, and let $A^
u$ be the integral closure of $A_{\mathrm{red}}$ in its total ring of fractions, the local reduced-normalization construction [def-weil-pbc-reduced-normalization]. There is a canonical isomorphism of $\kappa$-schemes
$$\operatorname{Proj}(\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak m}A)\ \cong\ \operatorname{Spec}(A^
u/\mathfrak m A^
u).$$
 Writing $C^
u	o C$ for its reduced normalization, this spectrum is canonically $C^
u	imes_C\operatorname{Spec}\kappa$. The algebra $A^
u/\mathfrak m A^
u$ is a separable quadratic $\kappa$-algebra: it is either $\kappa	imes\kappa$ or a separable field extension of $\kappa$ of degree two. The isomorphism is intrinsic to the pointed local ring and is natural under its isomorphisms; its two points after extending $\kappa$ to an algebraic closure correspond to the two branches of the normalized completed node. Associated graded rings and Proj are [def-weil-pbc-associated-graded-ring, def-nagata-affine-proj]; spectra are [def-weil-affine-spectrum].

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-separable-node-quadratic-completion] to obtain reducedness, Noetherianity, essential finite type and dimension one for A=O_C,x, together with the nondegenerate quadratic completion. Forget the algebra structure of its equivalence; associativity of multiplication identifies the two written quadratic equations. Use [lem-sfb-nodal-tangent-canonical-grading] for the canonical grading and degree-zero residue isomorphism.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-nodal-quadratic-tangent-comparison] to obtain i:Proj(gr_m A)≅Spec E, normalized on all allowed charts and natural, with a regular parameter f whose chart covers Proj and the quadratic residue alternative. Apply [lem-sfb-nodal-normalized-chart-uniqueness] to prove uniqueness and compatibility with the residue-field structural maps.

source.place: Tag 0CBT, omitted equivalence of constructions (2) and (3); Tags 0CBU and 0CBW for branches.

proof.text: Finite type over the field makes C locally Noetherian by [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft]. Apply [lem-sfb-reduced-normalization-local-fibre] for its canonical lift Spec B→C^ν and cartesian residue square. The universal property of the pullback gives the fibre isomorphism, with both required projection equations. These data form Comparison.

source.place: Tag 0CBT, omitted equivalence of constructions (2) and (3); Tags 0CBU and 0CBW for branches.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-nodal-geometric-branch-square]. Transport its cartesian square along i.symm on the Spec E corner, leaving the other three corners fixed. The induced isomorphism with the pullback is the required geometric branch isomorphism. Its second projection is the pullback equation; its first projection reduces using i.inv≫i.hom=id. Preserve the supplied representative formulas and cardinality two.
